purpose: Compact Skill Support summaries for first paint and no-JS deep links. Completing practice never marks a Roadmap task complete.

probation_hose_advancement.title: Hose Advancement (Probation)
probation_hose_advancement.summary: A short, correct attack-line evolution you can run on a quiet morning: pull, flake, charge, advance, reload.
probation_hose_advancement.why: Probation is where the company decides if you can be the backup firefighter without thinking.

probation_ppe_scba.title: PPE and SCBA Ready Check
probation_ppe_scba.summary: Be dressed correctly, on air when required, with a partner check — every time, not only when someone is watching.
probation_ppe_scba.why: Companies notice who is still clipping a coat at the curb.

probation_apparatus.title: Apparatus Familiarity
probation_apparatus.summary: Find the tool in the dark, explain what it is for, and put it back where the next person expects it.
probation_apparatus.why: ‘I don’t know this rig’ expires after about two shifts.

probation_radio.title: Portable Radio and Mayday Format
probation_radio.summary: Turn it on, get the right channel, talk short, and know the Mayday format before you need it.
probation_radio.why: A probationary firefighter with a dead radio is invisible. A probationary firefighter who cannot call a Mayday is in extra danger.

probation_hydrant.title: Hydrant Connection
probation_hydrant.summary: Make the hydrant the way THIS company makes it: adapters, slow open, kinks dressed, a real ‘water available’ report.
probation_hydrant.why: If the hydrant person fails, the whole engine fails. Probation often owns this job.

probation_ladders.title: Ground Ladder Basics
probation_ladders.summary: Carry, heel, raise, and lock a ladder for a simple objective without hitting wires.
probation_ladders.why: You will be the heel person. If you cannot heel, the tip person is in trouble.

probation_reset.title: Post-Call Reset
probation_reset.summary: After the run: people, air, hose, tools, and a ready apparatus — before anyone sits down for a hero sandwich.
probation_reset.why: The next tones will not wait for your recap. Probationary firefighters who reset without being asked get trusted.

probation_company_life.title: Company Life and Feedback
probation_company_life.summary: Be on time, ask for one correction, take it without drama, and keep a private learning log — no patient identifiers.
probation_company_life.why: Skill without coachability still fails probation. Coachability without skill fails the fire.

ff1_ppe.title: PPE Readiness and Donning
ff1_ppe.summary: Don complete structural PPE correctly, check interfaces, and be ready to go on air without skipping protection for speed.
ff1_ppe.why: Gear that is open, twisted, or incomplete is how firefighters get burned and inhale products of combustion on ‘ordinary’ jobs.

ff1_scba.title: SCBA Operations
ff1_scba.summary: Don and work on air, manage consumption, handle emergencies, and leave with a reserve — air is a tactical resource.
ff1_scba.why: Most Maydays have an air problem attached. SCBA skill is survival, not just a test station.

ff1_hose_advancement.title: Hose Advancement
ff1_hose_advancement.summary: Deploy, charge, and advance an attack line as a team with nozzle control, communication, and a working backup firefighter.
ff1_hose_advancement.why: Water at the right place, in a form you can still move, is the core engine-company product.

ff1_ground_ladders.title: Ground Ladders
ff1_ground_ladders.summary: Select, carry, raise, place, and climb a ground ladder for a stated objective: access, rescue, ventilation, or egress.
ff1_ground_ladders.why: A ladder in the right place is a firefighter’s second staircase. A ladder in the wrong place is a trip hazard that helps no one.

ff1_forcible_entry.title: Forcible Entry
ff1_forcible_entry.summary: Read the door, pick tools, control the door after it opens, and force only as much as the objective requires.
ff1_forcible_entry.why: The door is both an obstacle and a flow-path control device. How you force it changes the fire.

ff1_search.title: Primary Search
ff1_search.summary: Search with team integrity, orientation, a purpose, and a way out — then communicate what you found or did not find.
ff1_search.why: Search is a life-saving assignment that also kills firefighters who lose the wall, the partner, or the exit.

ff1_ventilation.title: Ventilation Support
ff1_ventilation.summary: Ventilation is a fire-behavior tool. Openings must match the attack, the search, and the chosen flow path — not habit.
ff1_ventilation.why: Wrong ventilation makes the fire bigger, faster, and closer to people. Timing is the skill.

ff1_water_supply.title: Water Supply Support
ff1_water_supply.summary: Catch a hydrant, manage supply hose, and support the engine as assigned — the pump operator cannot do this alone.
ff1_water_supply.why: Firefighter I water-supply work is how the engineer gets a chance to be good.

ff1_fire_attack.title: Fire Attack Fundamentals
ff1_fire_attack.summary: Apply an effective stream as part of a team: the right stream, the right place, coordinated with ventilation and search.
ff1_fire_attack.why: Cooling fuel and controlling the flow path is how room-and-contents fires stay room-and-contents fires.

ff1_communications_mayday.title: Communications and Mayday
ff1_communications_mayday.summary: Use the radio so people can help you: routine traffic, progress, and a Mayday that includes location, unit, and the problem.
ff1_communications_mayday.why: A silent firefighter in trouble is a body recovery. A clear Mayday is a rescue problem with a chance.

ff1_overhaul_salvage.title: Overhaul and Salvage
ff1_overhaul_salvage.summary: Find hidden fire without destroying evidence or people, and protect property that the fire did not already take.
ff1_overhaul_salvage.why: Rekindle, injuries during overhaul, and ruined belongings are preventable company failures.

ff2_ventilation.title: Coordinated Ventilation
ff2_ventilation.summary: Choose opening location and timing with suppression and search — not as a separate sport.
ff2_ventilation.why: Firefighter II is where you stop ‘taking the roof because we always do’ and start making the fire behave on purpose.

ff2_vehicle_extrication.title: Vehicle Extrication Support
ff2_vehicle_extrication.summary: Stabilize, create a work plan, and support patient access with approved tools — without becoming a victim of traffic or energy.
ff2_vehicle_extrication.why: Cars store energy. Traffic keeps moving. The patient is not helped by a rushed, unstabilized cut.

ff2_foam.title: Foam Operations
ff2_foam.summary: Match foam to the fuel, set up proportioning equipment correctly, and know when foam is the wrong tool.
ff2_foam.why: Wrong foam, wrong percentage, or a starved eductor wastes concentrate and fails to extinguish.

ff2_preplan.title: Preincident Survey
ff2_preplan.summary: Collect the information a company will wish it had at 2 a.m.: access, water, occupancy, systems, and special hazards.
ff2_preplan.why: First-due knowledge is a firefighting skill. Guessing a building in smoke is how people get trapped.

ff2_company_tactics.title: Company-Level Tactics
ff2_company_tactics.summary: Turn an incident objective into firefighter tasks, benchmarks, and a radio update without pretending to be command.
ff2_company_tactics.why: Firefighter II is the working supervisor of a task — not the IC, not a freelancer.

ff2_radio_reports.title: Condition and Progress Reports
ff2_radio_reports.summary: Give short CAN-style updates: conditions, actions, needs — so command can think.
ff2_radio_reports.why: Long stories clog the channel. Missing stories leave people in danger.

ff2_evidence_overhaul.title: Evidence-Aware Overhaul
ff2_evidence_overhaul.summary: Expose hidden fire while disturbing origin indicators as little as the fire problem allows.
ff2_evidence_overhaul.why: The investigation is often won or lost by the first companies with pike poles.

ff2_hose_testing.title: Hose and Equipment Service Testing
ff2_hose_testing.summary: Plan a safe hose/equipment service test: zones, documentation, failure criteria, and tagging out failures.
ff2_hose_testing.why: Burst hose on the fireground is a predictable maintenance failure. Testing is how you find it in the lot.

hazmat_ops_recognition.title: Recognition and Identification
hazmat_ops_recognition.summary: Use clues, markings, occupancy, and current references to identify likely hazards without becoming part of the release.
hazmat_ops_recognition.why: Wrong ID produces wrong isolation and dead firefighters. Guessing a product from a smell is not a tactic.

hazmat_ops_isolation.title: Isolation and Protective Actions
hazmat_ops_isolation.summary: Establish initial isolation, deny entry, and choose protective actions from current references and the AHJ plan.
hazmat_ops_isolation.why: Most lives at a HazMat scene are saved by keeping people out of the product, not by heroic entries.

hazmat_ops_erg.title: ERG Navigation
hazmat_ops_erg.summary: Find the material, the guide, isolation information, and emergency contacts quickly in the current ERG.
hazmat_ops_erg.why: A reference you cannot navigate under stress is a paperweight.

hazmat_ops_zones.title: Control Zones
hazmat_ops_zones.summary: Lay out hot/warm/cold concepts so work, decon, and command do not share the same puddle.
hazmat_ops_zones.why: If the cold zone is in the product, everyone is in the hot zone and nobody admitted it.

hazmat_ops_decon.title: Emergency Decontamination
hazmat_ops_decon.summary: Set up operations-level emergency/gross decon so people and equipment do not spread the problem.
hazmat_ops_decon.why: The second incident is the contaminated ambulance and the exposed firefighter who ‘only stepped in it.’

hazmat_ops_defensive.title: Defensive Control Options
hazmat_ops_defensive.summary: Choose defensive actions you are trained and authorized to do: dike, dam, divert, remote valve, vapor suppression — and stop at the ops boundary.
hazmat_ops_defensive.why: Operations level is not ‘almost a technician.’ Leaving your level is how people die in product.

hazmat_ops_ppe.title: PPE Limitations
hazmat_ops_ppe.summary: Know what department HazMat PPE actually protects against — and when structural firefighting gear is the wrong answer.
hazmat_ops_ppe.why: The wrong suit is a costume. Breakthrough, heat stress, and training limits kill.

hazmat_ops_radio_brief.title: HazMat Initial Radio Brief
hazmat_ops_radio_brief.summary: Give a concise first report: location, clues, wind, exposures, actions, resources, and a safe approach.
hazmat_ops_radio_brief.why: The second-due company will drive into the product if your first report was ‘we have a smell.’

do_pumper_hydrant_ops.title: Hydrant Operations
do_pumper_hydrant_ops.summary: Connect a reliable hydrant supply, manage intake pressure, watch residual, and communicate before changing demand.
do_pumper_hydrant_ops.why: Most urban structure fires succeed or fail on whether the first engine actually has the water the fire needs. Hydrant work is not just hooking a hose — it is reading the system while the incident changes.

do_pumper_pump_theory.title: Pump Theory
do_pumper_pump_theory.summary: Understand how a centrifugal fire pump makes pressure, why it needs water at the eye of the impeller, and what gauges are telling you.
do_pumper_pump_theory.why: Formulas fail in the street if the operator does not know what the machine is doing. Pump theory is how you recognize cavitation, loss of prime, and useless RPM.

do_pumper_apparatus_inspection.title: Daily Apparatus Inspection
do_pumper_apparatus_inspection.summary: Find the problem in the bay, not on the fireground. Fluids, warning systems, pump, tires, equipment, and documentation.
do_pumper_apparatus_inspection.why: Most ‘it died on the call’ stories started as a skipped check. Inspection is an operator skill, not busywork.

do_pumper_engage_pump.title: Engage Pump
do_pumper_engage_pump.summary: Position, shift to pump, confirm pump mode, tank-to-pump or supply, and a charged first line without guessing.
do_pumper_engage_pump.why: The first 60 seconds of pumping set up everything that follows. A missed shift confirmation is a dry line at the door.

do_pumper_friction_loss.title: Friction Loss and PDP
do_pumper_friction_loss.summary: Estimate pump discharge pressure from nozzle pressure, hose friction, elevation, and appliances — then sanity-check the number.
do_pumper_friction_loss.why: A wrong PDP either starves the nozzle or overpressures people and hose. The math is a starting point; the gauges and the nozzle firefighter tell you if it is working.

do_pumper_multiple_attack_lines.title: Multiple Attack Lines
do_pumper_multiple_attack_lines.summary: Keep pressure, supply, and communication stable when a second or third line opens or shuts.
do_pumper_multiple_attack_lines.why: The fire does not wait while you re-do math. Opening another line changes flow, residual, and every existing discharge.

do_pumper_master_streams.title: Master Stream Operations
do_pumper_master_streams.summary: High-flow devices need water, reaction awareness, supply, and a reason — not just a bigger nozzle.
do_pumper_master_streams.why: A master stream can overwhelm a hydrant, a pump, and a building. It is a tactical tool with a supply problem attached.

do_pumper_relay_pumping.title: Relay Pumping
do_pumper_relay_pumping.summary: Move water a long distance with more than one pump: roles, intake targets, communications, and failure recognition.
do_pumper_relay_pumping.why: Relays fail from silence and ego, not from math. Every engine needs a role, an intake target, and a way to say ‘hold.’

do_pumper_drafting.title: Drafting
do_pumper_drafting.summary: Build an airtight suction path, prime, lift water from a static source, and recognize cavitation and air leaks.
do_pumper_drafting.why: Drafting is unforgiving. One air leak or a fouled strainer turns a rural fire into a tank of regrets.

do_pumper_standpipe_fdc.title: Standpipe and FDC Operations
do_pumper_standpipe_fdc.summary: Supply a standpipe or sprinkler FDC with the right hose, the right pressure method, and a clear communication loop with the interior crew.
do_pumper_standpipe_fdc.why: High-rise and sprinklered buildings fail the first engine when the operator treats an FDC like a hydrant with extra hose. Elevation, system loss, and the people on the standpipe outlet all have to be in the same picture.

do_pumper_rural_tender.title: Rural Water and Tender Shuttle
do_pumper_rural_tender.summary: Keep fire flow coming when there is no hydrant: tank duration, fill and dump sites, shuttle math, and the radio loop that actually delivers water.
do_pumper_rural_tender.why: Rural fires run out of water in minutes if the first engine treats tank water as infinite. Shuttle success is cycle time and jobs — not how many tenders are ‘en route.’

do_pumper_apparatus_placement.title: Apparatus Placement
do_pumper_apparatus_placement.summary: Stop the engine where the hose, water, rescue path, later units, and a way out all still work — then set the brake and own that decision.
do_pumper_apparatus_placement.why: A bad spot is a permanent tactical problem. You can recut a line. You cannot un-park a blocked aerial or a hydrant you drove past with no plan.

do_pumper_troubleshooting.title: Pump and Supply Troubleshooting
do_pumper_troubleshooting.summary: Change one variable at a time: supply, valves, air, restrictions, cavitation, governor, then the discharge side.
do_pumper_troubleshooting.why: Panic makes operators twist everything. Method makes water come back.

fo1_initial_radio_report.title: Initial Radio Report
fo1_initial_radio_report.summary: From the seat, paint a picture: occupancy, conditions, actions, strategy, and what you need next — in a format later units can use.
fo1_initial_radio_report.why: The rest of the incident will copy your first 20 seconds. A vague ‘we have fire showing’ wastes staffing.

fo1_size_up.title: Size-Up and Risk
fo1_size_up.summary: Build a usable picture: life hazard, fire location, building, access, water, and what would change your mind.
fo1_size_up.why: Strategy without size-up is a guess with a radio.

fo1_strategy_tactics.title: Strategy and Tactics
fo1_strategy_tactics.summary: Pick a strategy you can staff, assign tactics that match it, and change both when the fire tells you to.
fo1_strategy_tactics.why: Offensive tactics under a defensive strategy (or the reverse) is how companies get stretched into bad air.

fo1_accountability.title: Assignments and Accountability
fo1_accountability.summary: Every member has a task, a location, and a way to be counted — especially when the plan changes.
fo1_accountability.why: Unassigned firefighters invent jobs in the worst air. Unaccounted firefighters become Maydays with no last location.

fo1_transfer_of_command.title: Transfer of Command
fo1_transfer_of_command.summary: Hand off a compact brief: situation, strategy, assignments, accountability, resources, hazards, and immediate needs.
fo1_transfer_of_command.why: A bad transfer creates two commanders and zero accountability.

fo1_coaching.title: Coaching and Crew Performance
fo1_coaching.summary: Correct a specific behavior with a private, factual conversation: what you saw, the standard, the impact, and the follow-up.
fo1_coaching.why: Officers who only yell in the bay never fix the thing that will hurt someone at 3 a.m.

fo1_documentation.title: Incident Documentation
fo1_documentation.summary: Write what happened in objective language: times, decisions, people (as required), and follow-up — without creative writing.
fo1_documentation.why: The report is how the organization learns, defends, and improves. A sloppy narrative becomes the official story.

fo1_risk_management.title: Risk Management
fo1_risk_management.summary: Name the risk, reduce it if you can, refuse what you cannot staff, and take care of the crew after the work.
fo1_risk_management.why: Company officers are the last people who can still say ‘we are not doing that’ before someone pays.

fo1_after_action.title: After-Action Review
fo1_after_action.summary: Run a short, blame-light review: what we intended, what happened, why, what to keep, and one change.
fo1_after_action.why: If the only review is yelling, the crew learns to hide. If there is no review, the next fire is a repeat.

fi1_objectives.title: Performance Objectives
fi1_objectives.summary: Turn a station skill into one observable objective: who, does what, under what conditions, to what standard.
fi1_objectives.why: If the objective is ‘understand hose,’ nobody can teach it or test it. If it is ‘advance a charged 1¾-inch line to a marked door in full PPE,’ you can.

fi1_delivery.title: Deliver Prepared Instruction
fi1_delivery.summary: Open, explain, check for understanding, and close — without drowning learners in slides.
fi1_delivery.why: A brilliant skill can still fail if the instructor rambles, skips the check, or never tells people what success looks like.

fi1_demonstration.title: Demonstrate, Practice, Coach
fi1_demonstration.summary: Show the skill correctly, let them practice, and coach the next rep with specific feedback — then fade the prompting.
fi1_demonstration.why: Talking about a ladder raise is not a ladder raise. Bad demos become departmental folklore.

fi1_training_safety.title: Training Safety Brief
fi1_training_safety.summary: Brief the evolution: objective, hazards, PPE, boundaries, stop signal, accountability, rehab, and the emergency plan.
fi1_training_safety.why: Most training LODDs looked like ‘just a drill.’ The brief is how you refuse to be casual.

fi1_evaluation.title: Skill Evaluation
fi1_evaluation.summary: Give the same directions, watch the same points, score what you saw, and close professionally — this is not a popularity contest.
fi1_evaluation.why: Inconsistent evaluators create unofficial standards and lawsuits. Fairness is a skill.

fi1_feedback.title: Specific Feedback
fi1_feedback.summary: Name the observed behavior, the standard, the effect, and the next repetition’s focus.
fi1_feedback.why: ‘Do better’ is not feedback. Neither is a personality review.

fi1_documentation.title: Training Records
fi1_documentation.summary: Complete attendance, objective, instructor, date/time, evaluation, and remediation fields so the record would survive an audit.
fi1_documentation.why: If it is not recorded, the organization cannot prove the training happened. That becomes a legal and ISO/accreditation problem.

fi1_adapt.title: Adapt Delivery, Keep the Standard
fi1_adapt.summary: Change explanation, pace, or demo for the learner in front of you without lowering the performance standard.
fi1_adapt.why: The job does not grade on a curve when the line is charged. Instruction can flex; the standard should not quietly disappear.
